# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Lazarus Landing for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## Green Hell The first survey crews logged LV-624 as a jungle world: hot, wet and loud from the riverbanks to the cave mouths. The name they gave it among themselves outlived every kinder name in the paperwork. Anything left out in the open here rots, rusts or gets eaten, usually in that order.
## The Landing - Weyland-Yutani raised the first domes on firm ground south of the river, where the jungle has a weaker grip on the soil. - The settlement was named [bold]Lazarus Landing[/bold]. The old hands say the first camp flooded out in its first wet season, and the crews dug it out of the mud and started again. - Research, Robotics and the hydroponics fields up north followed, tied together by the Nexus road. The Communications Dome and the Company's Dawnbreaker relay keep it talking to the sector.
## Under the Flag LV-624 lies in United Americas space and the colony lives under colonial law. The Colonial Marshal Bureau keeps the peace from the CMB precinct, the Colonial Administration signs the ordinances, and the USASF keeps a recruiters office for anyone who would rather wear a uniform than swing a machete. The Company keeps its own guards and its own Corporate Dome, and the lines between them have never been as clear as the charter makes them sound.
## Hard Lessons - The jungle takes people every year: lost on the river, hurt in the brush or turned around in the caves past the barrens. - A freighter came down hard north of the colony years ago. Her containers still lie scattered across the barrens, and salvage crews have picked them over ever since. Nobody has ever printed her full manifest. - The caves north-east of the colony, including the chamber the work crews call the [bold]Sand Temple[/bold], are posted off limits. The Herald has asked why more than once. We are still waiting for an answer.
## The Press The Herald began as a corkboard in the canteen, where hydroponics crews pinned up the names of anyone overdue from the jungle and crossed them off when they walked back in. It moved onto the net when the relays came up, and it still runs on the same rule: names, not numbers.
